#WATCH | India's cheetah conservation programme records another milestone as a two-and-a-half-year-old female cheetah brought from Botswana gives birth to four cubs in the wild.

Identified as KOMG 3, the cheetah is the first female from Botswana to give birth in India. She spent more than four months in the wild before delivering the cubs under natural conditions.

With the latest births, India's cheetah population has risen to 62, including 43 born in the country, Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav announced on November 20.

This is only the second recorded birth in the wild since Project Cheetah was launched in 2022. The previous instance was in April 2026, when an India-born female cheetah gave birth to four cubs at Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh.

India's cheetah reintroduction programme began in September 2022, after the species was declared extinct in the country in 1952. Kuno National Park has been the primary site for the programme.

Yadav credited project managers, veterinarians and frontline forest staff for their role in the conservation effort.

For a moment, if you sideline Coal India and look at RARE EARTH PERMANENT MAGNET MANUFACTURING.

What can we think about?

If you map the complete rare-earth permanent magnet value chain, there are 3 layers.

Upstream – Rare earth ore mining, mineral processing and separation, NdPr oxide production and the availability and processing of heavy rare earths such as dysprosium and terbium.

Midstream – NdPr oxide to rare-earth metal, metal to NdFeB alloy, strip casting and alloy processing, hydrogen decrepitation, jet milling, magnetic-field pressing, sintering, heat treatment, grain boundary diffusion, precision machining and surface coating.

Downstream – EV traction motors, wind turbine generators, industrial motors and BLDC fans, defence and aerospace systems, and consumer electronics.

Now, why should we look at this ecosystem?

India's estimated rare-earth permanent magnet demand is projected to reach around 8,220 tonnes annually by 2030.

Against this, the government has introduced a scheme with an outlay of ₹7,280 crore to establish 6,000 TPA of integrated sintered NdFeB magnet manufacturing capacity.

So, even if the entire proposed capacity comes up, it would still be below the projected domestic demand. This leaves room for additional domestic capacity, provided the economics and execution work.

But setting up magnet manufacturing facilities is only one part of the requirement.

Building this ecosystem will require several specialised capabilities, processes and equipment.

This is where the second order opportunities come in.

These include:

- Rare-earth metal production
- Specialised alloy manufacturing and strip casting
- Powder processing and precision equipment
- Hydrogen handling and inert-gas systems
- Magnetic-field pressing
- Vacuum furnaces, sintering and heat treatment
- Grain boundary diffusion
- Precision machining and surface coating
- Testing, inspection and qualification

There will also be requirements for specialised process chemicals, industrial gases, solvent extraction, industrial automation, process control, maintenance and magnet recycling.

But if you look at the entire chain, NdPr oxide availability is one of the important upstream dependencies.

For the proposed 6,000 TPA magnet capacity, the estimated NdPr oxide requirement is around 2,000 tonnes annually.

The government's scheme identifies up to 500 TPA of assured supply from IREL for selected beneficiaries.

So, additional sourcing and processing capabilities will be important if India wants to scale domestic production.

And this is not the only constraint. India will also need capabilities in oxide-to-metal conversion, alloy manufacturing, specialised processing equipment and customer qualification.

This is where I think the opportunity could emerge.

It may be in NdPr oxide-to-metal conversion, rare-earth alloy manufacturing or integrated sintered magnet manufacturing.

These are the capabilities India is specifically trying to establish.

There are already some interesting developments in this direction.

#AshviniRareEarth has established a pilot plant for NdPr metal production, #PGTech is working on molten salt electrolysis and #ARCI has established a pilot facility covering the process from strip-cast alloy to finished sintered magnets.

The companies that can be studied here include #Midwest, #20Microns, #MegathermInduction, #Electrotherm, #MIDHANI, #PTCIndustries, #PermanentMagnets and #Thermax.

We should also track IREL, NFTDC, ARCI, Ashvini Rare Earth, PG Tech and PolyProtic Chemicals for their roles in developing upstream and midstream capabilities.

However, their exposure is different.

Some are directly involved in magnet manufacturing or have participated in the manufacturing scheme. Others have capabilities in metallurgy, equipment, materials or downstream magnetic products that could potentially become relevant as the ecosystem develops.

The important thing is to understand where the spending will happen, which capabilities will be difficult to build and which companies can actually capture that spending as this ecosystem develops.

Mahanadi Coalfields produced 218.31 million tonnes of coal in FY26.

That represents:

🔹 21% of India’s domestic coal production
🔹 28.4% of Coal India’s total production
🔹 Nearly 34% of Coal India’s consolidated profit

How do you sustain a multi-decade infra boom without overloading the public balance sheet?
₹2.9 lakh crore set to be unlocked in FY27, a ~50% jump over FY26. ✅️

₹16.72 lakh crore five-year pipeline across 12 sectors under NMP 2.0 .

Asset monetisation is now a repeatable capex engine.

Instead of stretching sovereign finances for every greenfield project, the Centre is recycling operational brownfield assets,  combining lease/ concession revenues with committed PPP private capex to free fiscal space for fresh infrastructure. 

After delivering ~₹2 lakh crore (80% of target) in FY26, FY27 is tracking 80–90% of the ₹3.26 lakh crore target.
• Roads (~₹1 lakh crore): NHAI-led via BOT concessions (~₹60,000 crore) and InvITs, still prime paper for domestic and foreign institutions.

• Coal & Mining (~₹80,000 crore): Commercial block auctions, Coal India subsidiary stake dilutions, and mining lease/CL auctions.

Proceeds flow largely to states, partly to the Centre.

• Power & Ports (~₹50,000 crore each): Transmission network leasing in power; PPP berths and terminal concessions at major ports.

• Railways (~₹30,000 crore): Equity dilution in rail PSUs, land monetisation, and freight shed developments.

Build. Operationalise. Monetise. Reinvest.

That’s how you compound national infrastructure without straining fiscal headroom.

If you own a stock that listed in the last 3 years, check one number. Happy Forgings' promoters just sold 3.44% because of it.

The number is promoter holding. The rules don't let it stay above 75% for long.

The Ludhiana forging maker listed on 27 Dec 2023 at ₹850 a share. Its first shareholding filing after listing showed promoters at 78.60% and the public at 21.40%.

The listing rule: a company that lists with under 25% public holding gets 3 years from listing to reach 25%. Happy Forgings' 3 years are almost up.

For almost 3 years the stake barely moved. It was still 78.44% on 16 Nov 2026.

On 17 Nov, Paritosh Kumar, Ashish Garg and two family HUFs sold 32,47,750 shares. The company's 18 Nov filing says promoters now hold exactly 75.00%.

CNBC-TV18 reported a pre-open block of 16.33 lakh shares that day at an average ₹1,845, 2.7% below the previous close of ₹1,897.

Why it matters: a forced sale adds a fixed lump of supply on a known date. It tells you nothing new about orders, margins or demand for forgings.

What we don't know yet: who bought. What to watch: the December quarter shareholding filing, which should show it.

The takeaway: when a promoter sells, read the reason in the filing first. Sometimes it is the law, not a view on the business.

If a promoter sells only because a rule forces it, should that day's price move mean anything to you?

Not a recommendation. Do your own research.

5 years of going nowhere.
From ₹1,171 in late 2021 to ₹1,155 today (Nov 2026) - a negative return of ~1.4% over 5 years. Even on a 3 year basis, returns sit around a sluggish 7% CAGR with zero real compounding.
Everyone calls this internet classifieds giant a new age compounder & a safe tech proxy. Yet if you held it for half a decade, you rode a rollercoaster from ₹1,171 down to ₹700, up to ₹1,800 & right back below where you started.
Look check its numbers:

🚫Expensive on every metric: Trading at 45.2x P/E & 91x Price to Free Cash Flow while the industry median P/E sits at 15.6x. You are paying bubble prices for a mature job portal.
🚫Paper profits: TTM net profit looks huge at ₹2,212 cr, until you notice ₹1,472 cr of that is just Other Income from startup valuations & treasury. The core business makes less than half of what the headline shows.
🚫Terrible return on capital: Even with zero debt & 38% operating margins, ROE is stuck at 2.45% & ROCE is 3.45%. Over ₹46,000 cr of reserves sit locked in investments that barely earn anything for regular shareholders.
🚫Growth is cooling off: 5 year sales growth looked strong at 24%, but 3 year & trailing 12 month growth have dropped to 12 to 13%.

Great business, terrible stock returns. Never confuse a famous brand with a good entry price, otherwise your money is doing nothing but funding someone else's exit.

Nerodno jih je bilo gledati, kako so bruhali o svojem duševnem zdravju in travmah, medtem ko so izražali sočutje do gangsterjev in ničesar ne rekli za nedolžne ljudi, ki so jih ti gangsterji umorili, posilili in terorizirali.

Haitijci so protestirali za Bukeleja. Ljudje v Ekvadorju si želijo Bukeleja. Ljudje na Jamajki si želijo Bukeleja. Ljudje v Južni Afriki si želijo Bukeleja.

Ves svet je opazoval, kako se je Salvador iz prestolnice umorov na svetu spremenil v eno najvarnejših držav v Ameriki, in rekel, naj to storijo tudi tukaj.

Zapiranje kriminalcev ni nehumano. Ni slabo. Ni kruto. To je najboljši način za služenje pravičnosti, varnosti ter ohranjanje miru in reda.

Gangster, ki posili 12-letnico, si ne zasluži sočutja. Gangster, ki zažge avtobus, poln ljudi, si ne zasluži svetovanja za travme.
